title: Systems: flash-kernel SDPA for the 4 NoPE heads (is_causal, no float mask) in the causal training forward, ALiBi heads keep their bias, on the 136-fable MTP Lean incumbent
description: Speed lead from program.md (the ALiBi float attn_mask keeps SDPA off the flash kernel), systems work under Robbie's 2026-09-25 encouragement, no backlog id (P34 x P32 hybrid heads made cheaper): the slope-0 NoPE heads' bias is exactly causal, so in the unmasked training forward they run SDPA with is_causal=True (flash) while the 4 ALiBi heads keep their bias, the same function as 136-fable. More pretraining steps in the same 300 s wall-clock (and a faster uncached RL fine-tune forward) should give a slightly better-trained starting point for expert iteration.
hypothesis: The float (1, 8, T, T) ALiBi mask forces all 8 heads through the memory-efficient/math SDPA kernels, which do not skip the upper triangle and read a dense bias. Half the heads have slope 0, so their bias is just the causal mask; running them via flash with is_causal skips masked blocks and drops half the bias traffic. If attention is a sizeable share of the ~89 ms step at T~350 padded tokens, steps rise 5-15% at an identical function, and pretraining is step-limited (147-claude: fewer steps at the same epochs cost 30), so the extra steps should carry into RL.
expected_delta: -30 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central +3); pretrain steps ~3,550-3,900 per seed vs 136-fable's 3,370 mean. If steps rise <3%, the mechanism is falsified regardless of score

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, identical to 136-fable (features() returns (final hidden state, ALiBi bias) for the pretraining-only MTP module)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: systems only, same function as 136-fable: in the plain causal forward (pos, mask and caches all None: pretraining steps, val_loss, and any uncached unmasked forward) ALiBiGPT.features builds the (1, 4, T, T) bias for the 4 ALiBi heads only, and PeriLNBlock.attn (trunk blocks and the MTP block) splits SDPA: heads 1-4 get attn_mask=bias (as before), heads 5-8 (slope 0, whose bias was exactly 0 / -inf causal) run with is_causal=True and no mask, which lets SDPA pick the flash kernel; outputs are concatenated on the head axis. Sampling (pos/mask/caches given) keeps the unchanged full 8-head bias path. Parameters, optimizer, loss, schedule, batch and handoff unchanged
arch.n_params_detail: model: identical to 129-claude, 4,800,000 (vocab 107; CPU check model.n_params() == 4,800,000). MTP module (pretraining only, not on the model): 922,880 = PeriLNBlock 790,784 + proj 131,072 + 2 LayerNorms 1,024; pretraining trains 5,722,880 parameters in total, all under the 10M cap even if counted
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: identical to 136-fable (same module tree and state_dict keys)
arch.kv_cache: unchanged from 136-fable: cached/masked forwards take the original 8-head bias path

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial); the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (256,512) input proj) join the Muon group and its LayerNorm gains/biases and projection biases join AdamW, same lr, schedule and decay as the trunk
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock with CHANGED floor: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak (115-fable: 0.1 x peak). Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 follows the same factor, and so does its per-step decoupled decay lr * MUON_WD

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor CHANGED 0.1 -> 0.3); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 129's 24 hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (256,512; RMS shape scale sqrt(2)): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are unchanged

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1. The MTP module gets the same fork _init (normal 0.02, zero biases) followed by orthogonal_ on its 2D parameters (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so the (256,512) proj has element std 0.02); its LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0. Trunk RNG draws are identical to 129 up to the MTP module's construction, which happens after the trunk is built

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

systems.attention_kernel: NoPE heads: SDPA is_causal=True without attn_mask (flash-eligible: bf16, head dim 32, no dropout); ALiBi heads: SDPA with the (1, 4, T, T) float bias as before (non-flash). Previously all 8 heads took the float-bias path
systems.expected_steps: about 3,550-3,900 pretraining steps per seed vs 136-fable's 3,370 mean (+5-15%)
